description: The line plot illustrates the performance of four different methods—TACRED, TACRED-Revisit, Re-TACRED, and SemEval—measured by Micro F1 score (%) as the number of samples generated increases from K=8 to K=64. The x-axis, labeled "Number of Samples Generated," is scaled linearly with four discrete points: K=8, K=16, K=32, and K=64. The y-axis, labeled "Micro F1 (%)," is also linear and ranges from 25 to 50, with major gridlines at 25, 30, 35, 40, 45, and 50. The TACRED method (blue line with circle markers) shows a steady increase in performance, starting at approximately 23% at K=8 and rising to about 29% at K=64. The TACRED-Revisit method (orange line with triangle markers) follows a similar trend, starting at around 23% and peaking at approximately 31% at K=32 before slightly declining to about 30% at K=64. The Re-TACRED method (green line with diamond markers) demonstrates a significant increase, starting at roughly 35% at K=8, rising to about 39% at K=16, and then sharply increasing to a peak of approximately 50% at K=32, before slightly decreasing to around 48% at K=64. The SemEval method (red line with square markers) shows a consistent upward trend, starting at about 43% at K=8 and increasing to approximately 52% at K=64. All four lines exhibit a general upward trend in Micro F1 score as the number of generated samples increases.
